# Adrian Mag — Personal Academic Website

> Personal academic website of Adrian Mag, PhD researcher in theoretical
> seismology and inverse theory at the University of Oxford. The site
> contains long-form mathematical notes series on inverse problems and
> inference, plus publications, presentations, and CV.

Notes for LLMs: the notes pages are static HTML with mathematics written
in LaTeX (MathJax source is present verbatim in the raw HTML, delimited by
\( ... \) and \[ ... \]). Each notes series has a plain-text AI reading
companion describing its narrative arc, notation, intent, and guardrails
against common misreadings. Read the companion before helping a reader
with a page from that series.

## Notes series

- [My Take on SOLA](https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/sola/my-take-on-sola.html):
  Ten-act critical walkthrough of the SOLA method for linear inverse
  problems. Central claim: SOLA estimates properties through resolving
  kernels, not the desired target kernels, and without prior information
  the gap is unbounded.
  AI companion: https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/sola/ai-companion.txt

- [Think First, Discretize Later](https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/think-first/think-first-discretize-later.html):
  Eight-act argument that linear inverse problems must be formulated in
  function space (space, geometry, adjoint, prior measure) before
  discretization; the naive discretize-first posterior diverges under
  mesh refinement. Supplementary material for an EGU 2026 poster.
  AI companion: https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/think-first/ai-companion.txt

- [Bayes, Measure-Theoretically](https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/bayes/bayes-measure-theoretically.html):
  A tiny discrete inverse problem solved twice: by joint-table arithmetic
  and by measure-theoretic machinery (kernels, disintegration, posterior
  kernel). Same numbers, different language — the language that survives
  infinite dimensions.
  AI companion: https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/bayes/ai-companion.txt

- [Bayesian and Frequentist Inference](https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/frequentist/bayesian-frequentist.html):
  Five-part comparison built on one observation equation. Bayesian and
  frequentist schools construct different epistemological objects and
  license different statements; confidence-set coverage is pre-observation,
  following Neyman (1937).
  AI companion: https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/frequentist/ai-companion.txt

- [The Road to Conjugate Gradients](https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/cg/conjugate-gradient.html):
  Six-act derivation of the conjugate gradient method as a sequence of
  forced moves, from gradient descent onward, done in a real Hilbert
  space with the operator as a black box. Interactive descent panels;
  every claim carries verified, clickable citations.
  AI companion: https://adrian-mag.github.io/pages/research/overview/cg/ai-companion.txt
